summary.oneLiner: Akums navigated a challenging H1 FY26 to deliver strong Q4 recovery, driven by double-digit CDMO volume growth and the turning of Trade Generics EBITDA positive, while setting up significant optionality via a $25mn/year Zambia sovereign contract and EU commercial supplies starting FY28. The key inflection is the expected sharp reduction in API losses and the transition from domestic dependency to high-margin regulated market exports.
summary.business: Akums is a CDMO founded in 2004 that manufactures pharmaceutical formulations for over 1,400 Indian and multinational pharma and wellness companies, including 26 of the top 30 pharmaceutical companies in India, across more than 60 dosage forms. Beyond CDMO, the Company operates its own Domestic and International Branded Formulations businesses, a Trade Generics business, and an Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) business, serving pharmaceutical companies, FMCG companies, healthcare providers and government/institutional buyers.

CDMO: Dapagliflozin tablets (initial commercial CDMO supply to Switzerland)

endMarkets: Domestic Indian pharmaceutical market (pan-India, 28 states and 8 union territories)|Export markets across 72 countries|Africa (existing markets plus new Zambia joint-venture facility)|Europe (EU-GMP accredited facilities; commercial supplies to Switzerland)|Asia (extended footprint to support international growth)

currentContext.strengths: Largest India-focused CDMO by revenue, production capacity and clients served|Long-standing partnerships with 26 of the top 30 pharmaceutical companies in India and 1,400+ CDMO clients|Ownership of intellectual property for several manufacturing processes and deep formulation/process expertise|Large, growing in-house R&D capability (370+ scientists, 1,192 patents granted cumulatively, R&D spend at 3.2% of revenue) supporting new-formulation development|Global regulatory accreditations (WHO-GMP, EU-GMP) enabling access to regulated international markets|Diversified presence across the pharmaceutical value chain (CDMO, branded formulations, API) providing multiple growth levers while mitigating single-segment risk|Pan-India distribution network reaching urban and rural geographies
currentContext.strategies: Deepen core CDMO strengths and expand high-value/complex dosage capabilities (sterile injectables, hormones, beta-lactams) to capture premium outsourcing mandates and enhance margins through complex offerings|Expand international/regulated-market footprint through Europe (EU-GMP accredited plants, first major European CDMO formulation mandate) and Africa (Zambia joint venture) to shift from a domestic manufacturer with export exposure toward a global CDMO partner|Drive an innovation-led product pipeline via strengthened R&D, continued DCGI approvals, first-to-market and complex launches, and increased filings in regulated markets to drive portfolio premiumisation|Improve utilisation of newly ramped manufacturing capacities and drive scale efficiencies across sterile, oral solid and liquid dosage forms|Embed sustainability into the manufacturing ecosystem — standardise ESG-aligned sourcing practices, implement vendor performance analytics, integrate logistics with emissions monitoring, and enhance ESG disclosures|De-risk geographic concentration by creating a regional export hub for Southern Africa and strengthening relationships with sovereign institutions|The Board recommended a final plus special dividend for FY2025-26, payable out of the Company's profits and subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, indicating an intent to return a portion of profit to shareholders alongside continued reinvestment in the core manufacturing and CDMO business (organic capacity expansion and international JV/expansion activity) in the ordinary course of business; no separate, more detailed dividend-distribution-policy statement (e.g., a target payout ratio) is present in this bundle beyond the specific FY2025-26 recommendation.
currentContext.expansion: Akums operates 14 consolidated manufacturing facilities (11 CDMO plants and 3 API plants), clustered at Haridwar and Kotdwar (Uttarakhand) and Baddi (Himachal Pradesh) for CDMO/formulations, and at Sundran and Chachrauli (Punjab) and Barwala (Haryana) for API. During FY2025-26 the Company commenced operations at a new injectable manufacturing facility in Haridwar, strengthening sterile manufacturing capabilities, and ramped up newly commissioned Oncology and Steroid facilities. Consolidated CDMO capacity utilisation improved steadily from 24.6% in FY2023-24 to 39.4% in FY2024-25 and 42.9% in FY2025-26, while the API business operated at utilisation levels of 50%-84%; overall consolidated capacity utilisation stood at ~47%, which management said gives significant headroom to grow without substantial incremental capital investment. A total capital expenditure of Rs.2,220 Million was deployed during the year towards capacity expansion, equipment modernisation, infrastructure upgrades and regulatory compliance initiatives, with the largest share (Rs.519.07 Million) directed to the Akums-3 facility to strengthen production capabilities, install advanced manufacturing equipment and enhance operational efficiency. The Company also reported a ~15% productivity improvement during FY2025-26. Separately, during the year the Company entered into a Joint Venture with the Government of the Republic of Zambia for the establishment of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility, marking a strategic step in its global expansion.
currentContext.mdna: Structural industry shift from conventional generics to complex and differentiated dosage forms (sterile injectables, modified-release formulations), driven by pricing pressure in standard categories and rising demand from biologics, oncology and GLP-1 pipelines|Patent expiries worth USD 63.7 Billion between 2025-2029 creating a significant opportunity for complex generic development|Regulatory upgrades such as India's revised Schedule M framework accelerating quality-led industry consolidation, favouring manufacturers with advanced infrastructure and compliance capabilities|Outsourcing becoming structurally embedded in global pharmaceutical value chains, supporting continued CDMO demand|Sustained growth in global and Indian healthcare/wellness consumption: global pharmaceutical market projected to grow at an 8.19% CAGR to CY2034; Indian IPM reached Rs.2.42 lakh crore as of January 2026, growing 8.0% YoY with monthly growth accelerating to 10.21%|CDMO business delivered double-digit volume growth in FY2025-26, significantly outpacing broader IPM volume growth, with CDMO contributing 80% of total revenue|Participation in high-growth chronic therapies (cardiology, anti-diabetics, CNS, gastroenterology) through Akumentis Healthcare, and in the wellness segment through a US-NSF certified nutraceutical facility|10+ products in pipeline for European filings until FY28|CEP filings initiated for select APIs|Government of Zambia procurement commitment of USD 25 Million per annum for FY27 and FY28, providing a demand-assured gateway for the Zambia joint venture|Progress on the European CDMO contract with commencement of commercial supplies (Dapagliflozin and Rivaroxaban) to Europe/Switzerland

risks.risk: Global trade friction, tariff shifts and geopolitical realignment
risks.note: The MD&A's Global and Indian Economy overview repeatedly flags renewed trade frictions, geoeconomic fragmentation, evolving geopolitical developments and potential supply-side disruptions as sources of continued global uncertainty; Akums is actively expanding its export and international footprint (Europe, Africa/Zambia) and is therefore exposed to these external headwinds.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility and global supply-chain disruption
risks.note: The Indian Economy Outlook explicitly names commodity price volatility and global trade uncertainties as potential headwinds to India's growth trajectory, and the Global Economy section separately flags potential supply-side disruptions; both are relevant to Akums as an API/formulations manufacturer dependent on input costs and cross-border logistics.

risks.risk: Elevated public debt and fiscal pressure in advanced economies constraining global demand
risks.note: Cited in the Global Economy overview as a headwind to sustained global growth and monetary policy flexibility, which could dampen demand conditions in Akums' developed-market (European) expansion markets.

one-line thesis: Akums navigated a challenging H1 FY26 to deliver strong Q4 recovery, driven by double-digit CDMO volume growth and the turning of Trade Generics EBITDA positive, while setting up significant optionality via a $25mn/year Zambia sovereign contract and EU commercial supplies starting FY28. The key inflection is the expected sharp reduction in API losses and the transition from domestic dependency to high-margin regulated market exports.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 4,359cr (+5.8% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 1,158cr (+9.7% YoY). EBITDA: INR 522cr (+13.3% YoY), Margin 12.0% (vs 11.2% prior); Q4 EBITDA INR 152cr (+61.6% YoY), Margin 13.1%. PAT: INR 256cr (vs INR 344cr prior); decline due to absence of INR 106cr one-off deferred tax asset benefit seen in FY25. Normalized PBT grew 11.9% to INR 382cr. Order Book: Strong visibility with $25mn/year Zambia contract (FY27-28) and EUR 35mn/year EU contract (6 yrs from FY28). Net Debt: Net Cash position of INR 1,682cr; FCF INR 958cr.
guidance: Revenue: CDMO double-digit volume growth expected in H1 FY27; Domestic Formulations to grow at/above IPM (high single/low double digit); International Formulations to return to double-digit growth. Margins: CDMO margins to sustain ~13-14%; API losses to reduce sizably but may remain negative for full year FY27. Order Inflow: Zambia supplies commence Q2 FY27; EU commercial supplies from FY28. Capex: INR 300cr targeted for FY27.
order book & pipeline: Zambia: $25mn per annum for FY27 & FY28 (supplies from India), followed by local manufacturing ramp-up from FY29. EU CDMO: EUR 35mn per annum for 6 years (till 2032), commencing FY28. Domestic CDMO: Strong pipeline with 10+ products for European markets.
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO: Rev INR 3,485cr (+8.6% YoY), EBITDA INR 467cr (+2.9%); Q4 Rev INR 952cr (+13.4%), EBITDA INR 137cr (+54.9%). Domestic Branded: Rev INR 446cr (+2.9%), EBITDA INR 90cr (+17%); Q4 Rev declined 1.5%. Int'l Branded: Rev flat at INR 143cr, EBITDA +32.3% to INR 36cr; Q4 Rev -9.7%. Trade Generics: Rev INR 100cr (-13.2%), EBITDA turned positive at INR -10cr (vs -28cr); Q4 EBITDA +INR 1.4cr. API: Rev INR 184cr (-15.9%), EBITDA loss narrowed to INR -40cr (vs -44cr); Q4 loss widened to INR -12cr due to mix/volume.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Zambia JV: $45mn total capex (51% Akums), local production from FY29 targeting $200mn market. 2) EU Regulated Markets: Plant 2 accredited, dossier filing underway for 10+ products, commercial supply FY28. 3) Injectables: New facility ramping up (teens utilization), expected significant contribution in FY27. 4) Inorganic M&A: Evaluating niche business acquisitions using strong cash reserves.
margins & cost dynamics: CDMO model is cost-plus percentage margin; absolute profits fluctuate with API input costs. Recent API price hikes (single high-digits) benefit absolute margins despite soft YoY comparison. Gross margins supported by shift to complex dosage forms and regulated markets. Operating leverage from capacity utilization driving EBITDA expansion.
capex / expansion: FY26 Actual: INR 222cr. FY27 Guidance: INR 300cr. Focus on oral solids expansion, injectables ramp-up, Penem facility, and Zambia JV ($23mn Akums share).
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion (oral solids, injectables) and inorganic M&A in niche segments. Dividend: INR 1 final + INR 2 special (total INR 3/share). Strong FCF (INR 958cr) supports aggressive growth capex without debt.
risks & watch-items: 1) API Price Volatility: Cephalosporin and bulk API prices remain below peak levels, pressuring API segment profitability. 2) Geopolitical/Crude: Inflation in solvents/raw materials (though largely pass-through). 3) Execution Risk: Delays in EU commercialization or Zambia facility commissioning. 4) Regulatory: Schedule M implementation pace and inspection outcomes.
management quality / tone: Confident and pragmatic. Acknowledged FY26 as 'transitional' with H1 challenges but emphasized strong Q4 momentum. Clear focus on long-term value creation via regulated markets over short-term trade generic scale. Transparent on API losses and path to recovery.
non-obvious takeaways: The Trade Generics business was consciously shrunk to fix working capital cycles, not due to lack of demand; it is now a small, profitable niche. The EUR 200mn EU contract is for an established molecule with predictable volumes, de-risking the ramp-up. The Zambia deal includes a transition from export (FY27-28) to local manufacturing (FY29+), locking in long-term sovereign demand.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API price volatility and regulatory delays | Divis Laboratories | beneficiary | Med | Peers with strong regulated market exposure may see relative valuation re-rating as Akums validates the CDMO regulated market thesis. |
| Margin pressure in domestic formulations | Small-cap Unorganized Formulators | loser | High | Schedule M compliance costs and Akums' scale advantage in CDMO will likely consolidate market share away from smaller, non-compliant players. |

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
